text: Atorvastatin labeling includes myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. Patients should report unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness, particularly if accompanied by malaise or fever.
The most common adverse reactions associated with amoxicillin include nausea, diarrhea, and rash. Serious hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis have been reported.
Metformin labeling warns about lactic acidosis and use in renal impairment. Acute kidney injury, dehydration, sepsis, and hypoxic states may increase risk and require interruption of metformin.
Ibuprofen and other NSAIDs can cause gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, perforation, renal toxicity, hypersensitivity reactions, and serious skin reactions.
Aspirin labeling includes bleeding risk, gastrointestinal bleeding, dyspepsia, nausea, vomiting, bronchospasm, urticaria, and hypersensitivity reactions.
